## Objective

Unzip the downloaded census file and open 2018-SA1-dataset-individual-part-3a-total-NZ_updated_16-7-20, you will see a tab for Territorial authority. Join the 2018 paid employee field to the spatial data and make a basic map. Hint, you may need to make a new `.csv` file from the data.

# Load the Data

## Loading the CSV

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
nz_csv <- read_csv("Statistical Area 1 dataset for Census 2018-total-New Zealand_updated_4-11-21/2018_Cleaned.csv")  
```

## Load the shapefile

```{r}
library(sf)
#st_read turns a spatial dataset from computer and turns it into an sf object
nz_shp <- st_read("statsnz-territorial-authority-2018-generalised-SHP/territorial-authority-2018-generalised.shp")
```

To get a summary of the data held within the shapefile data (attribute table) enter the following:

```{r}
summary(nz_shp)
```

To have a quick look what the shapefile looks like enter the following:

```{r}
plot(st_geometry(nz_shp))
```

```{r}
library(sf)
nz_shp %>% 
  st_geometry() %>%
  plot()
```

### Check the attribute table

In the environment tab, click on the nz_shp. It will open up an attribute table like QGIS.

## Review CSV

```{r}
names(nz_csv)
```

**Check Row count:**

```{r}
tail(nz_csv)
```

## Join SHP & CSV

auto complete column names: **Autocomplete with `$`:** type the object name and a dollar sign, then press Tab:

```{r}
nz_shp_join <- nz_shp%>%
  merge(.,
        nz_csv,
        by.x= "TA2018_V1_", 
        by.y="Area_Code")
```

## Check to see if it joined properly

```{r}
nz_shp_join%>%
  head(., n=10)

```

## Add a new column calculating percentage of paid employees out of total employed people

```{r}
nz_shp_join <- nz_shp_join %>%
  mutate(paid_emp_pct = (`2018_PaidEmployee` / `2018_GTotal2`) * 100)
```

Double checking the result:

```{r}
summary(nz_shp_join$paid_emp_pct)
```

# Making a Thematic Map

## Make a map showing 2018 paid employees

```{r}
library(tmap)
```

```{r}
tmap_mode("plot")
# change the fill to your column name if different
nz_shp_join %>%
  qtm(.,fill = "paid_emp_pct")
```

```{r}
install.packages("rmapshaper")
```

```{r}
nz_map <- nz_shp_join %>%
  filter(TA2018_V1_!= "999") %>%
  rmapshaper::ms_simplify(keep = 0.05)
```

```{r, fig.width=5, fig.height=7}
tmap_mode("plot")

tm_shape(nz_map) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "paid_emp_pct",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
      values = "carto.mint",
      style = "jenks",
      n = 5
    ),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(
      title = "Paid employees (%)",
      title.size = 0.9,
      text.size = 0.8,
      position = tm_pos_in("right", "bottom")
    ),
    col = "grey40",
    lwd = 0.3
  ) +
  tm_title("Paid Employees as a Share of the Employed Population, 2018", size = 1.2) +
  tm_layout(
    bg.color = "lightblue",
    frame = FALSE,
    text.fontfamily = "Questrial"
  ) +
  tm_credits("Source: Stats NZ, 2018 Census. Employed census usually resident population aged 15+.\nAuthor: Elodie Nix, October 2026",
             position = tm_pos_out("center", "bottom", pos.h = "left"),
             size = 0.6,
             color = "grey10")
```

# Export the Data

With the 999 area deleted :

```{r}
nz_map %>%
  st_write(.,
           here::here("Week1_Homework", "nz_employment.gpkg"),
           layer = "nz_2018_employment",
           delete_dsn = TRUE)
```

With the 999 area still in it:

```{r}
nz_shp_join %>%
  filter(TA2018_V1_!= "999") %>%
  st_write(.,
           here::here("Week1_Homework", "nz_employment.gpkg"),
           layer = "nz_2018_employment",
           delete_dsn = TRUE)
```

# Export with the original CSV

```{r}
library(readr)
library(RSQLite)

con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(),
                 dbname = here::here("Week1_Homework", "nz_employment.gpkg"))
```

```{r}
Hidecon %>%
  dbListTables()
```

```{r}
con %>%
  dbWriteTable(.,
               "nz_csv1",
               nz_csv,
               overwrite=TRUE)

con %>% 
  dbDisconnect()
```
